root_cause.text: The IPA v5.0+ GSI `GENERIC_CMD` register definition used incorrect bit masks in `drivers/net/ipa/reg/gsi_reg-v5.0.c`, so the driver encoded command fields at the wrong offsets and wrote malformed hardware commands.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `GENERIC_CHID` from `GENMASK(9, 5)` to `GENMASK(12, 5)`, `GENERIC_EE` from `GENMASK(13, 10)` to `GENMASK(16, 13)`, and adds the missing `GENERIC_PARAMS = GENMASK(31, 24)` field, with the commit message stating the masks were not matching the documented hardware layout and this caused a WARN when sending “stop” to MPSS while IPA was up.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The IPA v5.0+ GSI `GENERIC_CMD` register definition used incorrect bit masks in `drivers/net/ipa/reg/gsi_reg-v5.0.c`, so the driver encoded command fields at the wrong offsets and wrote malformed hardware commands.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `GENERIC_CHID` from `GENMASK(9, 5)` to `GENMASK(12, 5)`, `GENERIC_EE` from `GENMASK(13, 10)` to `GENMASK(16, 13)`, and adds the missing `GENERIC_PARAMS = GENMASK(31, 24)` field, with the commit message stating the masks were not matching the documented hardware layout and this caused a WARN when sending “stop” to MPSS while IPA was up.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the generic command field layout to match the correct register format and support the added parameters field.
intent_record.what: In the `reg_generic_cmd_fmask` array, the bitmask for `GENERIC_CHID` was expanded from bits 9:5 to 12:5, the bitmask for `GENERIC_EE` was expanded from bits 13:10 to 16:13, the reserved-bit comment was updated from bits 14-31 to bits 17-23, and a new `GENERIC_PARAMS` field was added using bits 31:24.
intent_record.how: This changes the decoded/encoded layout of the generic command register so it can carry wider channel and execution-environment values and additionally include a parameters byte, affecting how command values are constructed and interpreted at runtime.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the generic command field layout to match the correct register format and support the added parameters field.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes the GSI GENERIC_CMD register field layout/masks and adds the missing parameters field, which addresses malformed command encoding at the wrong offsets.

candidates.rationale: This field mask assigns the opcode to bits 4:0, which is part of the incorrect pre-fix layout. The root cause is that the GENERIC_CMD register fields were encoded at the wrong offsets, causing malformed hardware commands.
This channel ID mask uses bits 9:5 in the pre-fix definition, contributing to the incorrect GENERIC_CMD field layout and mis-encoding command fields.
This execution-environment mask places the field at bits 13:10 in the pre-fix definition. The bug stems from these incorrect bit masks shifting command fields to the wrong offsets.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix mask assigns GENERIC_OPCODE to bits 4:0, which is part of the incorrect GENERIC_CMD field layout. The driver therefore encoded the opcode at the wrong offset, contributing directly to malformed hardware commands.

This pre-fix mask places GENERIC_CHID in bits 9:5, but the register definition was supposed to use different offsets. This incorrect placement caused command fields to be encoded in the wrong positions.
This pre-fix mask assigns GENERIC_EE to bits 13:10 as part of the wrong GENERIC_CMD layout. That misalignment shifted the field to an incorrect offset, leading to malformed hardware command encoding.

Author: Alex Elder <elder@kernel.org>

    net: ipa: add IPA v5.0 GSI register definitions
    
    Add the definitions of GSI register offsets and fields for IPA v5.0.
    These are used for the SDX65 SoC.  Increase the maximum channel and
    event ring counts supported by the driver, so those implemented by
    the SDX65 are supported.
    
    Signed-off-by: Alex Elder <elder@linaro.org>
    Signed-off-by:
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the IPA v5.0+ GSI GENERIC_CMD register definition using incorrect bit masks/offsets. In this snippet, the GENERIC_CMD definition is present and explicitly defines the fields as `[GENERIC_OPCODE] = GENMASK(4, 0), [GENERIC_CHID] = GENMASK(9, 5), [GENERIC_EE] = GENMASK(13, 10)`, with the register registered via `REG_FIELDS(GENERIC_CMD, generic_cmd, 0x00025018 + 0x12000 * GSI_EE_AP);`. However, the snippet does not show any prior incorrect definition, nor any evidence that these masks are wrong relative to the hardware spec; it simply introduces the v5.0 register table. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not demonstrably present from this code alone, and there is no fix visible here because this commit is the initial addition of the definition rather than a corrective change.
